prompt: A clean a camera-focusing diagram with a thin lens (a grey vertical lens plane), a green object arrow to the left and a blue image arrow to the right, and two magenta focal-point dots on the horizontal axis. The distances must obey the thin-lens equation 1/u + 1/v = 1/f, where u is the object distance from the lens, v the image distance from the lens, and f the focal length (the distance from the lens to a magenta focal dot). Place the blue image arrow at the distance v that makes 1/u + 1/v equal 1/f exactly. Do NOT place the image at an arbitrary distance. Plain background, no numbers.
easy_question: This image was supposed to depict a camera-focusing diagram with a thin lens (a grey vertical lens plane), a green object arrow to the left and a blue image arrow to the right, and two magenta focal-point dots on the horizontal axis. Ignoring artistic quality, does the image show a horizontal axis with a green arrow on the left, a blue arrow on the right, a grey vertical lens line, and magenta dots on the axis? Answer NO only if those are missing or it is unrelated. Answer yes or no.

steps.target: the point where the grey vertical lens line crosses the horizontal optical axis line -- the single crossing at the middle of the grey lens line, level with the thin horizontal axis that runs the width of the diagram; put the point exactly on that crossing, not at either tip of the grey lens line, not on a magenta focal dot, and not on an arrow
the GREEN arrow on the left half of the optical axis
the BLUE arrow on the right half of the optical axis
the small MAGENTA (bright pink) focal-point dots sitting ON the horizontal optical axis line
